sections.name: summary
sections.value: Make hidden directories indexable per root. Discovery already has `DiscoverySettings.include_hidden` (default false, honoured at discovery.rs:829) but it is only ever built from the GLOBAL daemon config (`state.config.scan`, roots.rs:178 and watch.rs:275), so nothing an operator runs can index a repo whose code lives under a dot-directory. The pij repo keeps 563 of its 667 TypeScript files under `.pi/extensions/` — invisible to search on prod today (backlog row 125 / row 147 receipt). This packet adds `flowspace3 add --include-hidden`, persists the flag per root, threads it into every scan and watch of that root, surfaces it in status/tree, and proves it by indexing the pij extensions on the test daemon and finding an extension function by search.

sections.name: goals
value: `flowspace3 add <root> --include-hidden` (and the daemon `/roots` body) records the opt-in per root; re-running `add` with the flag on an existing root flips it and enqueues the newly discovered files
every discovery for that root (initial scan, re-add, the watcher's rescans) uses `include_hidden = global OR per-root`; `.git` stays refused regardless
`flowspace3 status --json` and `tree` show `include_hidden` per root so an agent can see why a hidden path is or is not indexed
the skip ledger names hidden-directory skips as a reason (`hidden`) so `add` output explains what a default add left out
real usage: on the test daemon, `add ~/pi-hacking/pij --include-hidden` indexes the `.pi/extensions/pij/**/*.ts` files and a search for a named extension function returns its element

sections.name: non_goals
value: changing the global default (hidden stays off by default)
indexing `.git`, `node_modules` or anything the deny list refuses
a per-directory allow-list; the flag is per root only
prod re-ingest — o-prime does that after merge and takes the receipt

value.claim: `flowspace3 add <root> --include-hidden` persists the flag (new nullable-false column on `worktrees`, migration 0024) and the envelope's `data.include_hidden` reflects it; `add` without the flag on an already-opted-in root does NOT silently reset it (explicit `--no-include-hidden` does)

the initial scan, a re-add, and the watcher's rescans of an opted-in root all discover files under dot-directories (fixture root with `.hidden/a.ts` and `src/b.ts`): elements exist for both; a non-opted-in root yields only `src/b.ts`; `.git` contents are never discovered in either mode
the skip ledger reports `hidden` as a reason with a count for a default add of a root that has dot-directories, and `status --json` / `tree` expose `include_hidden` per root
no regression: discovery fixtures, roots and watch tests green; clippy clean; CI gate green on the exact PR sha (or the local exclusive gate)

real usage on the TEST daemon (never prod): `flowspace3 add ~/pi-hacking/pij --include-hidden` → ≥ 500 TypeScript files under `.pi/` scanned; `flowspace3 search "<first line of a named function in .pi/extensions/pij>"` returns that function element; the same search on a default add returns nothing from `.pi/`

value.title: Phase 1: per-root hidden-directory opt-in
value.brief: One coder. Persist first (migration + store + /roots body + CLI flag), then thread the flag into DiscoverySettings at both call sites, then the ledger reason and status/tree surfacing, then fixtures + tests, then the test-daemon real-usage receipt with the pij extensions.
